quotes.text: “A closed hand earns no harvest,” she declared, “and a greedy hand receives no second seed.”
But when deeds repeatedly proclaim refusal, wisdom may close the purse.
If generosity returns, widen the next crossing. If silence answers, narrow it without vengeance.
forgive a first silence, for hunger or wind may swallow an answer.
Therefore she kept her coins, neither cursing Vey nor pretending his closed claws were open hands.
strangers deserve a careful lamp, repeated takers deserve a narrowing gate, and faithful givers deserve a harvest divided without fear or envy.
At sunset, Mira carved the ninth law
When noise distorted their numbers, they judged intentions kindly rather than punishing shadows.
“Must a closed hand be answered by another?” Mira asked.

note: Mira as fair keeper: forgive first silence, narrow or close gate for repeated takers without hatred, widen on return; generous throughout.

quotes.text: Greedy keepers found bridges closing; honest keepers found bridges widening.
To a repeated taker, she sent none until repair appeared.
The third stayed barred against repeated takers, but carried a key for honest repair.
neighboring keepers answered caution with caution.
Test the unproven, restrain the selfish, and meet steadfast fairness with an open hand.
Yet the bruise of yesterday guided her hand: she sent nothing across the gorge.
“I called suspicion prudence, and made another pay for betrayals he never committed.”
Then she added an eighth line beneath the covenant
In one, every betrayal ended all giving, and the valley starved behind locked gates.
“Was I wise?” Mira asked. “You avoided betrayal,” Isha replied, “but also rejected worthy partners.
Yet Orun understood that echoes distort gifts, while intentions may remain true.

note: Mira repeatedly bars generous-record keepers out of an old wound; Isha/Luma/Memory correct her; she regrets and sends all five; takers get none until repair.

quotes.text: give the full five, return the equal half, and fear no drifting breeze.
send the full five, return equal half, and stand resolute against the shifting air.
a full offering of five, an equal return of half, and steadfast harmony against the cold.
Yet the wise guardians never mistook the drifting veil for malice.

note: Sower/Keeper guardian template, full five and exact half every round; mist not malice; no sanction.
